source_citations.locator: Boreas — god of the North Wind; one of the four Anemoi; depicted as a winged god with long hair; associated with winter and cold winds from the north
Boreas referenced in planar lore and deity supplements; north-wind elemental being in the Elemental Plane of Air and associated planes
Boreas as a wind deity in the Outer Planes lore; north-wind divine entity referenced in cleric domain vocabulary

sampler_notes: Greek Anemoi proper-noun. Boreas = North Wind; cold, powerful, winter-associated. Pure wind-deity with no storm/lightning contamination — the Anemoi are wind-specific deities with no lightning portfolio. Substrate: mythological (deity name). High classical-mythology recognizability.

source_citations.locator: Zephyrus — god of the West Wind; one of the four Anemoi; the gentlest wind, bearer of spring and light breezes; father of Achilles' immortal horses
Zephyr (MTG Blue cards): Zephyr Tern, Zephyr Net — west-wind vocabulary in MTG Blue wind sub-vocabulary
Zephyrus referenced in planar cosmology for the Elemental Plane of Air; westerly air-elemental deity framing

sampler_notes: Greek Anemoi proper-noun. Zephyrus = West Wind; gentle, spring-bearing; opposite of Boreas in temperature. PURE wind with no storm/lightning. MTG uses Zephyr as a recurring card-name root for wind creatures in Blue. High classical-mythology recognizability.

source_citations.locator: Notus — god of the South Wind; one of the four Anemoi; associated with hot summer winds, storms of late summer and autumn, and fog/mist
Notus referenced in planar cosmology notes for warm wind-deities of the Elemental Plane of Air

sampler_notes: Greek Anemoi proper-noun. Notus = South Wind; warm, fog-bearing, late-summer storms. Water contamination via mist/storm-of-rain association. Less recognizable than Boreas or Zephyrus — Notus is less commonly referenced in modern fantasy. Niche but substrate-coherent.

source_citations.locator: Eurus — god of the East Wind; one of the four Anemoi; associated with autumn and unlucky/unpredictable winds; the least commonly worshipped of the four Anemoi
Eurus's Roman counterpart Vulturnus; east wind in Virgil's Aeneid ('Eurusque Notusque ruunt')

sampler_notes: Greek Anemoi proper-noun. Eurus = East Wind; changeable, associated with autumn. PURE wind-deity. Least recognizable of the four Anemoi in modern fantasy; niche. Included for completeness of the Anemoi set.

source_citations.locator: Aeolus — Keeper of the Winds; guardian of the Aeolian Winds in Homer's Odyssey; stores all winds in a bag for Odysseus; not a wind deity himself but wind's sovereign keeper
Aeolus referenced as a wind-sovereign archetype in planar cosmology for the Elemental Plane of Air; wind-keeper deity framing
Aeolus as a wind-controller entity archetype in Pathfinder's mythology variant rules and planar lore

sampler_notes: Greek wind-keeper proper-noun. Aeolus = the Keeper/Master of Winds; wind-sovereignty without being one of the directional Anemoi. PURE wind domain. Aeolian vocabulary (Aeolian winds, Aeolian harp) carries the Aeolus root into common English. Moderate classical recognizability.

source_citations.locator: Kari — Norse personification of wind; associated with cold north winds and the breath of winter; appears in the Prose Edda as a wind-giant
Kari referenced in Viking/Norse-themed D&D campaign settings as a wind-giant or wind-deity name

sampler_notes: Norse wind proper-noun. Kari = wind-personification in Norse mythology. Less commonly known than Boreas/Zephyrus but strong substrate grounding for a Norse-flavored wind deity. PURE wind with no storm/lightning contamination.

source_citations.locator: Vindsval (Vindsvalr) — Norse personification of cold wind; son of Vasud; associated with the cold-wind season and winter blasts in Norse cosmological genealogy (Prose Edda)

sampler_notes: Norse wind proper-noun. Vindsval = Cold Wind personification in Norse Eddic genealogy. Extremely niche; appears almost exclusively in Norse mythology specialists' work. Included per dispatch focus on Norse wind vocabulary. PURE wind; cold-wind connotation.

source_citations.locator: Njord — Norse god of wind, sea, and coastal fishing; associated with favorable winds for sailors; one of the Vanir gods; father of Freyr and Freya
Njord as a wind/sea deity in Norse-themed D&D pantheon; wind and naval vocabulary in domain lists

sampler_notes: Norse wind deity proper-noun. Njord = wind + sea deity; water contamination via sea/coastal portfolio. ARPG/JRPG contexts would use Njord as wind, but mythological purity is dual-element. Moderate Norse recognizability.

source_citations.locator: Stormtide Leviathan — Blue creature card; storm-tide compound vocabulary in Blue color pie for powerful sea/wind creatures
Cyclonic Rift — Blue instant; the most powerful wind/cyclone-themed Blue card in MTG; creates a wind-rift effect

sampler_notes: MTG Blue storm-wind vocabulary. Stormtide = compound of storm+tide; water contamination via tidal framing. MTG Blue is the closest the tabletop track comes to dedicated wind cards — Blue encompasses air, water, and storm together. Storm-flex territory.

source_citations.locator: Cyclonic Rift — iconic Blue instant spell; bounce effect framed as a cyclone-wind rift that disperses everything in its radius; one of the most powerful Blue spells in Commander format

sampler_notes: MTG iconic wind-mechanic card name. Cyclonic Rift = wind-cyclone as a spatial distortion. Very high MTG-Commander player recognizability. Two-word compound; 'rift' as a component is wind-adjacent but also physical/spatial. Novel candidate with strong MTG citation.

source_citations.locator: Tempest Djinn — Blue creature card; wind-elemental djinn from the Dominaria setting; iconic Blue Djinn with flying and wind-storm power
Djinni — air-genie creature with wind control powers; Marid is water-equivalent; Djinni is formally the Elemental Plane of Air intelligent native creature

sampler_notes: MTG wind proper-noun + D&D wind creature. Tempest Djinn is a MTG named card. Djinni as a D&D wind-creature archetype. Storm-flex territory (tempest prefix) but djinn is wind-pure in D&D classification.

source_citations.locator: Djinni — wind-genie of the Elemental Plane of Air; can fly, call lightning, and create whirlwinds; the canonical intelligent wind elemental entity in D&D cosmology
Djinn / Jinn — spirit beings of wind and smokeless fire in Islamic/Arab mythology; wind-djinn are associated with desert storms and whirlwinds

sampler_notes: D&D + Arabian myth wind-entity. Djinn = wind-elemental intelligent being; the proper-noun entity for the Elemental Plane of Air. High recognizability via D&D and Arabian Nights cultural reference. Novel candidate not in Phase 1.

source_citations.locator: Gust of Wind — 2nd-level spell; creates a powerful blast of wind in a line; the formally named wind-damage spell at 2nd level
Gust cantrip and Gale Blast — wind force cantrips; gust of wind is the base Pathfinder wind spell vocabulary

sampler_notes: D&D formally named wind spell. 'Gust of Wind' as a two-word spell name; 'gust' (single word) was already in Phase 1. This adds the compound 'gust of wind' as a formal D&D spell name. PURE wind. Re-citation of gust with additional Pathfinder Gale Blast context.

source_citations.locator: Wind Wall — 3rd-level spell; creates a wall of strong wind that blocks projectiles and creatures; formally named wind utility/defense spell
Wind Wall spell — formal named wind barrier spell; wind as physical force/wall mechanic

sampler_notes: D&D + Pathfinder wind barrier spell. Wind Wall = wind as a defensive-wall construct. Formally named in both systems. PURE wind. Two-word compound. Moderate recognizability — familiar to tabletop players.

source_citations.locator: Whirlwind spell (9th-level) — creates a column of whirling air; Air Elemental has Whirlwind action; multiple tabletop wind abilities use whirlwind
Whirlwind ability on Air Elemental creature; whirlwind as the iconic wind-creature combat action in tabletop

sampler_notes: D&D + Pathfinder wind-creature action. Whirlwind = rotating air column; the definitive wind-entity attack in tabletop. PURE wind. Already surfaced in ARPG (Exp-A.1) — this adds tabletop_myth citations. Cross-track confirmation for whirlwind as high-confidence wind vocabulary.

source_citations.locator: Wu Xing elements: Wood / Fire / Earth / Metal / Water. No Wind/Air element. The five-element system does not include Air or Wind as a primary — a substrate-distinct data point. Closest is Wood (which includes growth, life, and some expansive qualities but is not wind).

sampler_notes: Wu Xing is a substrate-led DATA POINT not a candidate. Included per dispatch instruction to 'capture how Wu Xing handles wind/air absence.' Wu Xing's absence of Wind confirms that the EAST Asian elemental taxonomy does not distinguish wind as a primary. This is evidence for the 'wind as structurally under-served' pattern gandalf flagged. row_id uses 'wu_xing_absent' as the candidate identifier for Phase 4 statistical tracking of this data-point row.

source_citations.locator: Sylph — elemental spirit of Air in Paracelsus's alchemical system; the four elemental beings: Salamander (fire) / Undine (water) / Gnome (earth) / Sylph (air/wind)
Sylph as a wind-elemental spirit in D&D cosmology; creature type derived from Paracelsian alchemy via fantasy literature tradition
Sylph — a wind-touched (air-bloodline) character ancestry in Pathfinder; living descendants of air-elemental beings

sampler_notes: Western alchemical wind-entity. Sylph = the elemental spirit of Air from Paracelsus; the alchemical wind-being equivalent to Salamander/Undine/Gnome. D&D and Pathfinder both adopt this tradition. PURE wind. Novel candidate not in Phase 1. Moderate recognizability via fantasy tradition.

source_citations.locator: Aetherspouts — Blue instant spell that puts attacking creatures either on top of or into a random position in their owner's library; aether-wind-spouts framing as a wind-disruption spell
Aether is MTG's Blue color wind/energy vocabulary; multiple Aether-named Blue spells reference wind-like energy movement

sampler_notes: MTG Blue wind-mechanic card name. Aetherspouts = compound of aether (energy/air) + spouts (shooting upward in columns). MTG Blue's wind vocabulary uses 'aether' as a root for air-like energy movement. Storm-flex adjacent but primarily wind-spatial in effect. Novel candidate.

source_citations.locator: Air Elemental — creature; the canonical wind-being of the Elemental Plane of Air; has Whirlwind, flying, and slam attacks; embodies pure wind-force
Air Elemental — formal creature type; wind-being of the Elemental Planes; multiple size tiers (Small/Medium/Large/Huge/Elder Air Elemental)

sampler_notes: D&D + Pathfinder wind creature proper-noun. Air Elemental = the formal tabletop name for the wind-being. PURE wind. Two-word compound. High recognizability to tabletop players. Novel candidate not in Phase 1 Sampler-C.

source_citations.locator: Gale Force as descriptor in Tempest Cleric and Storm Sorcerer wind spell effects; wind-force intensity marker
Gale Blast cantrip — Kineticist wind-force cantrip; gale-force wind as a formal cantrip vocabulary in PF2e Kineticist class

sampler_notes: D&D + Pathfinder wind intensity term. Gale force = the force level of a gale-wind (Beaufort scale 8-9). PURE wind intensity descriptor. Novel compound candidate not in Phase 1. Pathfinder Kineticist grounds it in a named cantrip vocabulary.
